reviewerErrorAtV1.disclosure: I accepted v1 at 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX. Codex found both a blocker and a SHOULD-FIX and was right on both. These are different failures and I record them separately.

blockerMissed.what: v1 marked OBL-2 capable-of-riding G01-G05. OBL-2 is DR-101's evidence-cell fragment 'gate harnesses DR-G01–G05' — the obligation is the harnesses themselves. Those five identifiers are named but not authored, so OBL-2's remainder includes authoring harness specifications, which D-056's Eligibility gate 2 expressly excludes from a splittable remainder.
blockerMissed.howIMissedIt: My v1 verdict recorded, approvingly, that 'all five harness cells begin named:'. I treated named as sufficient for an execution remainder and never asked whether authoring was still owed. The excluding rule was already in my working knowledge from earlier reviews in this session; I did not apply it to the one obligation whose subject matter is the harnesses.

shouldFixMissed.what: v1 gave a single executionObligationOwnerToday of 'Architecture + release engineering' for remainders riding five gates whose live owner cells differ, including G05's Component publisher + release.
shouldFixMissed.howIMissedIt: This is the worse of the two, because I found it and then talked myself out of it. I drafted this exact finding, then checked DR-101's row owner cell, saw it matched byte-for-byte, and withdrew the finding — recording the withdrawal in my verdict as a virtue under the heading that the answer to pressure is more verification.
shouldFixMissed.whyThatReasoningWasWrong: The matching row owner was an adjacent fact, not a test of the claim. The claim at issue was who owns the execution remainder for obligations that ride five specific gates, and the operative owners for that are the gate cells. A check that confirms a different proposition cannot refute a finding. I used a confirming lookup to kill a correct objection and then presented the kill as rigour.
shouldFixMissed.correctionAdopted: A verification must address the finding's own proposition. Where a claim spans several gates, the gate cells are the evidence; the row owner is a separate fact that neither confirms nor refutes it.

asymmetryAudit.question: If OBL-2 is leftover because G01-G05 are unauthored, why are OBL-1, OBL-D-INV, OBL-D-LAY and OBL-D3 capable-of-riding those same unauthored gates?
asymmetryAudit.whyItMatters: This is the obvious attack on the repair. If the distinction does not hold, the fix would be arbitrary and the other four would be leftover too.
asymmetryAudit.answer: It holds, and it follows from DR-101's own cell text. The evidence cell has two members: 'Reviewed closure inventory and dependency graph' (OBL-1) and 'gate harnesses DR-G01–G05' (OBL-2). OBL-2's subject matter is the harnesses, so its remainder is authoring them — excluded by Eligibility gate 2. OBL-1 and the three decision obligations are properties that v16 already specifies, whose remainder is measurement at named identifiers; that is the same shape as the DR-102 precedent, where classes ride a named-not-authored gate. The authoring obligation is not erased by that reading — it is tracked separately as OBL-2 and correctly marked leftover, and OBL-1's reason says in terms that it does not claim OBL-2's specifications are authored.
asymmetryAudit.consequenceIsConservative: Either way DR-101 is not eligible: with OBL-2, OD-101-1 and OD-101-2 leftover, gates 2 and 3 fail, which doesNotCloseLeftoverAlone states.

consideredAndDeclined.item: OBL-2 lists DR-G01–G05 under existingGate while being not-capable-of-riding, where OBL-D1 and OBL-D2 use existingGate none for their leftover status
consideredAndDeclined.whyDeclined: The field carries two senses across the array — gates at issue versus gates that own the remainder — but nothing false follows and three independent fields mark OBL-2 as leftover. Naming the five is also more informative than none, since authoring specifications for exactly those five is the closure condition. Charging a modelling nuance that improves the reader's information would be padding, which after two misses is its own failure mode.

coordinatorSummary: ACCEPT at 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX, with no advisories. Fifteen attacks run, none landed. Read the disclosure first: I accepted v1 at 0 and 0 and Codex was right twice. The blocker is that OBL-2 is DR-101's evidence-cell fragment 'gate harnesses DR-G01–G05' — the obligation is the harnesses — and those five identifiers are named but unauthored, so its remainder includes authoring, which D-056's gate 2 excludes. My v1 verdict actually recorded, approvingly, that all five harness cells begin 'named:', and I never asked whether authoring was still owed. The SHOULD-FIX is worse, because I found it and withdrew it: I drafted the finding that a single collapsed owner cannot stand for five gates whose owners differ, then saw that the string matched DR-101's row owner and dropped it, recording the withdrawal as rigour. The matching row owner was an adjacent fact, not a test of the claim; a confirming lookup cannot refute a finding about a different proposition. Both repairs land, and I verified them against primary bytes. OBL-2 is now leftoverDesign true, not-capable-of-riding, listed in summary.leftoverDesign, with its closure condition named as independently reviewed harness specifications. Its authority citation to D-056 turn-2 Decision clause 5 is precise — I nearly charged it as a misattribution because my first pattern match hit Eligibility gate 5, the MF-6 edit, but the pinned draft carries two numbered lists and Decision clause 5 reads 'Authoring fixtures and harness specifications remains lawful design work now. Execution remains qualification.' The owner repair is byte-exact: all five live cells reproduce in liveGateOwners and in each obligation's gateOwners, with keys matching that obligation's own gate list, and the row owner retained under its own distinct key. The obvious attack on the repair is why the other four obligations may ride the same unauthored gates; it fails, because the distinction comes from DR-101's own cell text, where OBL-2 alone is the harness member while the others are properties v16 specifies whose remainder is measurement — the DR-102 shape. Coverage still equals v16's seven-obligation decomposition, partitioned three leftover and four riding with empty intersection; required-now stays 26; all ten digests reproduce; every prohibition token is a refusal; and the artifact expressly declines to retarget D-159's fresh gates-2/3 holding for DR-117.
